contract: The road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that coming to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has begun, and not the state of lying inside the region afterwards. It states no direction of entry, no carrier the road user came through, no speed and no place within the region. Not a stand-in for: lying within the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still inside; the carrier or the way the road user came from, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or a leaving of the region.

elements.span: comes to overlap a structure region at the observation
elements.justification: rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is exactly the overlap of the footprint with the region argument at the observation; the kind of the region is the caller's, since the formal is a region variable the caller binds.

elements.span: did not overlap it at the observation before
elements.justification: the same relation read at the previous observation, which the formula language's 'rises' construct ('phi here and not at the previous observation') states over it; no other atom is read, so the event is the rise of that occupancy and nothing else.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint is clear of the junction polygon at one scene and overlaps it at the next: the concept is true at that next scene.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at both scenes: it is already inside, so the concept is false at the later scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not report whether the car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at the earlier scene, so whether the overlap has just begun is unknown.

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop, the driver shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'enters an intersection' is the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'), on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'); rel.occupies anchors the entry to the subject's own footprint ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') rather than any junction of the scene, and is the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs. 'a traffic-control signal' is DEF-NRS-484A-290, 'any official traffic-control device, whether manually, electrically or mechanically operated, placed or erected by a public authority or railroad, by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed': dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head' with states circular_green/circular_yellow/circular_red and the rest, the only device atom that alternately directs traffic to stop or proceed, and its 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered' carries 'which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered' word for word. 'controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', read on the same intersection the subject enters. 'but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection' is dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: the duty reads where the signal controls, not where a halt is due, and the halt's place is read in ob1 from its own marks. dev.traffic_signal is a device, not a sign, so no sign atom is claimed here. drv.motion.region_entry is not a stand-in for lying within the junction: the words fix the inoperative state to the instant of entry, so the entry event, not the occupancy, is what the condition is read at.

'the driver of the vehicle' singles out no further road user: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes 'driver' the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology's section on what is not an atom reads 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds the vehicle whose entry t1 reads. The class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom and never expanded into the classes it covers; the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle' to the same atom.

'shall stop' is the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 defines, 'complete cessation from movement', which drv.motion.standstill carries with the speed tolerance its contract names. 'at a clearly marked stop line' is st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device'; st.entrance_of ties it to the subject's own approach, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before', and st.lane_enters gives that carrier 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the line read is the one marking the entrance the subject enters by and never a line merely near it. st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over ('the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection'), rel.occupies the anchor that makes it the subject's own carrier. 'before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection' is st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', again tied by st.entrance_of, with the near side read as the crossing marking that entrance. prim.region_offset_along gives the side the subject is on, 'the signed distance from a road user's reference point to a structure region, measured along a carrier's designated direction', with st.lane_direction the direction it is measured along, and st.region_geometry the distance between the subject's body and the mark ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), which is what the stop-point tolerance bounds; the primitive's own inputs are not claimed beside it, and st.region_geometry is claimed for that distance, not for the primitive. 'at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is st.sight_along_way, 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation ... the smaller of the two directions', which is the view of traffic approaching on the crossing way from where the subject stands; st.on_way and st.highway bind that way ('the public way a structure region lies on'; 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). 'approaching traffic' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-285 defines, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', admitted as ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and claimed as one atom. st.sight_along_way is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen (rel.visible): the words require a view of the way, whether or not anyone is on it, which is what this atom and not that relation carries. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, and the three places are read in the order the words give them.

applicability: The subject vehicle enters an intersection (its footprint comes to overlap the junction region at the observation) and, at that entry observation, a traffic-control signal governs that intersection, is installed with its vehicular faces uncovered, and is inoperative.
obligation: Before that entry the subject must have come to a complete halt at the place the words name, in their order. The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier the subject occupies whose entrance end is that intersection. The place is the stop line recorded as marking that carrier; where the carrier's stop lines are observed and none marks it, the crosswalk recorded as marking that carrier; where neither is marked, the point on that carrier nearest the intersection at which the sight along the crossing way, in the lesser of its two directions, is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. A halt counts at the place when the subject's speed is at or below p.standstill_speed_tolerance while the distance between its body and the mark is at most p.stop_point_tolerance and it has not yet passed the mark, the side being read by the sign of prim.region_offset_along along the carrier's designated direction; a halt whose footprint already overlaps the intersection is not at the place. The search for the halt runs back from the entry observation and ends at the start of that approach -- the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, was off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance -- or at the previous entry of the same subject into the same intersection, and at nothing else: not at another junction, not at the first observation of the recording, not at a distance travelled. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without it the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end, because the history the bound needs begins before the recording or because the carrier's association with the mark or the carrier's direction is not observed, the duty is unknown. Where the stop line's entrances are observed and exclude the subject's carrier, the place is read from the next words in order and the duty is not unknown on that ground.

narrowings.why: 'shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection' is read through the conduct the same sentence and the next one prescribe -- the halt at the place and, in the second node, the cautious proceeding with its yielding -- and not through a stop-sign device: no stop sign is present in the scene, and reading one in would make the rule turn on a device the trace does not show.

'a clearly marked stop line' is read as the stop line the scene represents: the line's presence is the evidence of its clear marking, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes neither which place governs nor the halt and its timing.

'the through highway' is read as the highway the subject's approach crosses at that intersection: DEF-NRS-484A-275 makes a through highway one at whose entrances traffic is required by law to yield in obedience to a stop sign, a yield sign or other device, which is a legal designation no feature of a scene with an inoperative signal displays; the words' purpose here is the view of the traffic the subject must give way to, and that traffic approaches on the crossing way.

'has a view of approaching traffic' is read as the sight along the crossing way reaching at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance in the lesser of its two directions, and not as the driver's actual perception, which no trace carries.

'the driver of the vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car approaches a four-way junction whose signal heads are installed, uncovered and dark with no valid indication. A stop line is recorded as marking the lane the car occupies, the lane's entrance end is that junction, and the car crosses the line and enters the junction without its speed ever falling to the standstill tolerance anywhere on the approach from the line's upstream zone onward. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and the same inoperative signal. The car halts with its speed at zero while its body is within the stop-point tolerance of the stop line marking its lane and short of the line, then moves off and enters the junction. The scene contains no other road user, and the verdict is still decided.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same junction, but the signal governing it shows a steady circular red and is not inoperative. The car enters the junction without halting: the trigger does not hold, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car enters the junction without halting, the signal is installed and uncovered, but the source does not report whether the head is showing a valid indication, so whether it was inoperative at the entry is unknown and the rule reports unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A junction with the same inoperative signal where the lane's stop lines and crosswalks are observed and none marks the car's lane. The car halts, with its speed at zero, on its lane at the point nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing way reaches the view distance, then enters: the third place in the words' order governs and the duty is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and inoperative signal, with no stop line but a marked crosswalk recorded as marking the car's lane. The car slows to a crawl above the standstill tolerance before the crosswalk and rolls into the junction: the second place in the words' order governs and no halt is found on the approach.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already between the stop line and the junction, inside the line's stopping zone, and the car then enters the junction while the signal is inoperative. No halt is recorded, and the recording contains neither the start of the approach upstream of the line nor a previous entry of the car into that junction, so no recorded act and no visible end of the search decides the verdict.
scenarios.boundary: the stretch of the approach upstream of the stop line's stopping zone, at which the car entered that zone, lies before the first observation of the recording

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the complete cessation from movement DEF-NRS-484A-255 requires, set at the noise floor of a speed channel at rest.
param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which a halt counts as at the place the words name -- the stop line, the crosswalk or the view point -- covering the width of the marking and the position error of the body outline.
param_proposals.source: Marking-geometry and localisation practice: a transverse line about half a metre wide plus the position error of a body outline.

param_proposals.name: p.intersecting_way_view_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for approaching traffic to be seen before the crossing is begun.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight-distance tables for a crossing manoeuvre at urban approach speeds.

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,

the driver of the vehicle shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver
shall proceed cautiously,
yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: The same words as in the first node of this line take the same atoms. 'a vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and claimed as one atom. 'enters an intersection' is drv.motion.region_entry ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation') on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'), anchored by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') so that the junction read is the subject's own. 'a traffic-control signal ... installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head' with the 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered', the only device atom by which traffic is 'alternately directed to stop or proceed' as DEF-NRS-484A-290 requires; 'controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself'; 'is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection' is dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and the place of the halt is read in c1 from its own marks.

'such a stop' refers to the halt the previous sentence requires, and the condition carries that halt with every qualification the referring words keep: the same subject, the same place and the same order before the entry. The halt itself is drv.motion.standstill, which carries DEF-NRS-484A-255's 'complete cessation from movement' within the speed tolerance its contract names. The place is carried as the previous sentence states it: st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') or st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), each tied to the subject's own approach by st.entrance_of ('the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before') and st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), with st.travel_region the kind that carrier quantifier ranges over and rel.occupies the anchor to the subject's own footprint; else the point at which st.sight_along_way ('the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen') reaches the view distance, on the way st.on_way and st.highway bind. prim.region_offset_along gives the side along the carrier's designated direction st.lane_direction, and st.region_geometry the distance between the subject's body and the mark that the stop-point tolerance bounds. A weaker fact -- a halt anywhere, or a halt at another junction -- would not be the stop the words refer to, so the full qualification is carried here and the defining words are marked sibling only because the duty they state belongs to the other node.

'the driver' is the driver of the same vehicle the trigger reads; DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, whose class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom.

'vehicles' is DEF-NRS-484A-320, the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom for the road users quantified over inside the obligation. 'which have previously completed a stop' is drv.motion.standstill read at an earlier observation ('complete cessation from movement' within the speed tolerance), on a carrier whose entrance end is the same junction: st.lane_enters gives that entrance relation, st.travel_region the kind its carrier quantifier ranges over, rel.occupies the anchor to that other road user's own footprint. 'or are within the intersection' is rel.occupies on a region of kind st.intersection, the relation whose contract is exactly a footprint overlapping the junction region. 'yielding' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right of one vehicle 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not entering the junction while such a road user is within it -- drv.motion.region_entry is the entry event -- and by not closing on it, which rel.surface_gap ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies ... zero when they touch or overlap'), prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance measure under constant velocities within the horizon, with kin.speed the subject's own speed and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') the outcome the precedence is there to prevent. rel.surface_gap is not a stand-in for an order of arrival, which the words carry themselves through the earlier halt and the present occupancy; rel.contact is not a stand-in for a near miss, which is why the closest-approach primitives are claimed beside it.

operationalizations.convention: A low-speed stopping-distance convention bounds the caution: moving off from a required halt, the subject's speed where it enters and crosses the junction is held at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed, the speed at which a vehicle can halt within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to; the degree of the hazard enters through the conflict-avoidance convention, the closest approach under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon staying clear of p.yield_min_clearance, so that the bound moves with the proximity and the closing speed of the road users the same sentence names rather than switching on their presence alone.

applicability: The subject vehicle enters an intersection governed by a traffic-control signal that is installed, uncovered and inoperative at that entry, and at an earlier observation on the same approach the subject came to a complete halt at the place the first sentence names -- the stop line marking its approach carrier, else the crosswalk marking it, else the point at which the sight along the crossing way reaches p.intersecting_way_view_distance. The halt is searched for back from the entry to the start of that approach or to the subject's previous entry into the same junction, as the first node of this line states it; where that history begins before the recording the condition, and so the rule, is unknown.
obligation: From that entry on, while the subject is moving across or within the intersection, it must proceed cautiously -- its speed at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed -- and must grant precedence to every road user of the vehicle aggregate that either completed a halt earlier on a carrier whose entrance end is the same junction or lies within the junction at the observation: the subject must not enter the junction at an observation at which such a road user lies within it, must not come into contact with it, and must not let its closest approach to it under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon fall below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'yielding' is read as granting precedence in the three observable ways the right-of-way definition's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' admits on a trace: no entry into the junction while such a road user is within it, no contact, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance. A driver's deference that shows in none of these is outside what a trace can check.

'have previously completed a stop' is read as a halt at an earlier observation of the recording by that road user on a carrier whose entrance end is the same junction: the words give no place for the other road user's halt, and the junction's own entrances are the places at which such a halt is owed.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts at the stop line of its lane at a junction whose signal heads are installed, uncovered and dark, then accelerates into the junction at 8 m/s while a van that halted a moment earlier at the opposite entrance is already within the junction region: the subject enters while the van lies inside, and its speed is above the cautious bound.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and inoperative signal. The car halts at its stop line and then crosses the junction at 3 m/s. No other road user is in the scene at all, so nothing is owed precedence and the verdict is still decided.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same junction, the same dark heads, but the car never halts anywhere on its approach before entering the junction: the condition that it made such a stop does not hold, so this rule is not engaged and only the first node of the line judges the conduct.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at its stop line and moves off into the junction, but the source does not report whether the other road user's footprint overlaps the junction region, so whether a road user was within the intersection when the subject entered is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and inoperative signal. The car halts at its stop line, a van that halted earlier at the opposite entrance is within the junction, and the car stays at rest until the van has left the junction region, then crosses at 3 m/s with a closest approach well clear of the clearance bound.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at its stop line, then crosses the junction at 3 m/s, below the cautious bound, but passes within half a metre of a van already within the junction, the closest approach under constant velocities falling below the clearance bound within the horizon: precedence is not granted even though the speed is low.

param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.source: Marking-geometry and localisation practice: a transverse line about half a metre wide plus the position error of a body outline.

param_proposals.name: p.intersecting_way_view_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for approaching traffic to be seen before the crossing is begun.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight-distance tables for a crossing manoeuvre at urban approach speeds.

param_proposals.name: p.cautious_proceed_max_speed
param_proposals.convention: Low-speed stopping-distance convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle moving off from a required halt into a junction can be brought to rest within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to, taken as the 10 mph figure design practice uses for a stop-controlled entry.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping-sight-distance table at low design speeds, and the MUTCD practice of treating a stop-controlled entry as a crawl speed.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching an intersection
shall yield the right-of-way to a vehicle which has entered the intersection from a different highway.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: 'The driver of a vehicle' names no road user beyond the vehicle: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the person who drives or is in actual physical control of it, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle. Its class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), claimed as one atom and never expanded; the mapping index maps the same words to the same atom.

The ontology fixes what approaching an intersection is: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters)'. st.lane_enters is 'the relation: the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over ('a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection'), st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges') the junction itself, and rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own. The approach is read from the map and the junction, never from the subject's velocity or heading: st.lane_enters is 'entry topology ... never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity', so a subject at rest or backing on such a carrier is still approaching that junction.

'a vehicle' is again DEF-NRS-484A-320, the admitted aggregate claimed as one atom, for the road user quantified over inside the obligation. 'which has entered the intersection' is drv.motion.region_entry ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation') on the same region of kind st.intersection the trigger binds, together with rel.occupies for its lying there since that entry. 'from a different highway' reads the way of the carrier it entered by: st.lane_enters gives the carrier whose entrance end is that junction, st.travel_region the kind that quantifier ranges over, st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on', and st.highway the way itself, 'the entire public width between its boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority', as DEF-NRS-484A-095 defines it; the way so read is compared with the way of the subject's own approach carrier, which is what 'different' requires. 'shall yield the right-of-way' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not entering the junction while that road user lies within it (drv.motion.region_entry read on the subject), by not coming into contact with it (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap'), and by keeping its closest approach clear, which rel.surface_gap ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies ... zero when they touch or overlap'), prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance measure under constant velocities within the horizon, with kin.speed the subject's own speed. rel.surface_gap is not a stand-in for an order of arrival: the order is carried by the other road user's entry event itself. st.lane_enters is not a stand-in for the subject's presence in the junction, which rel.occupies carries.

'official traffic-control devices' is DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device not inconsistent with chapters 484A to 484E ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'. The definition's three included kinds are claimed by the ontology's own device and marking atoms: the signals by dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head'), dev.lane_control_signal, dev.pedestrian_signal, dev.crossing_warning_signal and dev.railway_signal_or_gate ('the devices at a level crossing'); the signs by dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt'), dev.yield_sign, dev.regulatory_sign ('a point regulation by catalogue code'), dev.zone_sign and dev.speed_limit_sign; the markings by st.lane_marking ('per side of a lane: type ... colour ...') and st.centre_line ('the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway'); and the temporary devices by dev.temporary_traffic_control ('cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers'). 'at intersections controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', read on the junction the subject approaches or on the approach carrier it occupies, which rel.occupies, st.travel_region and st.lane_enters bind to the subject's own approach so that a device governing some other junction of the scene does not excuse the duty. dev.regulatory_sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre or a road feature, and none is read as one here: only the presence of such a device governing this junction is read.

'vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions' is read exactly as the ontology directs: rel.oncoming is 'not a stand-in for the direction a road user approaches from -- that is read through the carrier it approaches through, any carrier st.lane_enters admits, whose entrance end is the intersection, and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction) at the same instant'. So each of the two vehicles occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is the same st.intersection (st.lane_enters), and the designated directions of the two carriers are opposed: the cosine of the angle between them is at or below the negative of p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance, the atom being read normalised as its contract states. The classes are the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. A turn that changes the current headings does not change the carriers, which is why the carriers' directions and not the bodies' headings are read.

'is making a left turn' is the manoeuvre drv.motion.left_turn denotes: 'the road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning ... the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle ... to the left'. It is read on whichever of the two vehicles the words allow ('one of the vehicles'), which includes the subject. The concept states the turning of the body only, and no signal or declared intention stands in for it; the intention the same sentence also names is carried separately, as the words join the two by 'intending to or is making'.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn to the left at the region named as the declaration's target

applicability: The subject vehicle is approaching an intersection: it occupies a carrier whose entrance end is that junction. The duty does not apply where an official traffic-control device governs that junction or the subject's approach carrier -- unless either node of subsection 4 is engaged for the subject at that junction, which suspends that exception -- and it does not apply where the subject and another vehicle of the aggregate each occupy a carrier entering that junction whose designated directions are opposed and either of them is declared to intend a left turn at that junction or is making a left turn.
obligation: At every observation on that approach the subject must grant precedence to every vehicle of the aggregate that has entered that junction from a carrier lying on a highway other than the one carrying the subject's approach: the subject must not enter the junction at an observation at which such a vehicle lies within it, must not come into contact with it, and must not let its closest approach to it under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon fall below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'shall yield the right-of-way' is read as granting precedence in the three observable ways the definition's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' admits on a trace: no entry into the junction while the other vehicle lies within it, no contact, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance. A deference that shows in none of these is outside what a trace can check.

'has entered the intersection' is read as an entry event of that vehicle into the junction at or before the judged observation together with its lying within the junction since: the words give precedence to a vehicle already in the junction, and a vehicle that has entered and left no longer competes for it.

'official' is read as the presence of the device on the road: the ontology makes the feature's presence the observable evidence of its official status, and a placement by a public authority is nothing a scene displays.
'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An unsignalised, unsigned crossing of two highways. A car occupies a lane whose entrance end is the junction; a van has already entered the junction from a lane lying on the other highway and is within it. The car drives on and its footprint comes to overlap the junction while the van is still inside.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same unsignalised crossing. The car occupies the approach lane and crosses the junction, and no other road user is present in the scene at any observation: nothing has entered the junction from another highway, so the duty is discharged and the verdict is decided with the subject alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car is travelling along a highway far from any junction: it occupies no carrier whose entrance end is an intersection, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A van has entered the unsignalised junction from the crossing highway, but the source does not report which way the van's entry carrier lies on, so whether it entered from a different highway is unknown and the rule reports unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same geometry, but a traffic signal governs the junction and shows a circular green for the car's approach while the van is within the junction. The section does not apply at a junction controlled by an official traffic-control device, and no node of subsection 4 is engaged because the signal is operative.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The same signal-controlled junction, but the heads are installed, uncovered and dark, so subsection 4 is engaged for the car: the device exception is suspended, the section applies again, and the car enters the junction while the van, which entered from the crossing highway, is within it.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: An unsignalised junction at which the car and a van occupy carriers entering it whose designated directions are opposed, and the source declares the van's current plan to be a left turn at that junction. The section does not apply to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions when one of them intends a left turn.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two directions still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees; its negative is the bound at which two directions are read as opposed.
param_proposals.source: The thirty-degree sector convention used for same-direction and opposed-direction tests in traffic conflict analysis.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_onset_yaw_rate
param_proposals.convention: Manoeuvre-onset convention: the rate of change of heading above which a body is read as turning rather than running straight, set above the yaw noise of a vehicle holding its lane.
param_proposals.source: Yaw-rate channel noise and lane-keeping figures from instrumented-vehicle studies.

param_proposals.name: p.left_turn_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn-recognition convention: the heading change accumulated since the onset at which a turn to the left is recognized as made, rather than as a lane change or a bend taken.
param_proposals.source: Manoeuvre-recognition practice: half the ninety-degree heading change of a right-angle junction turn.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.

segmentation.text: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways
at approximately the same time,
the driver of the vehicle on the left
shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: 'two vehicles' are two road users of the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, admitted as the aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and claimed as one atom for both. 'enter an intersection' is drv.motion.region_entry ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'), read for each of the two on one and the same region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'), with rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the anchor to each road user's own footprint and the kind-ranging relation the junction quantifier needs. 'from different highways' reads the way of the carrier each entered by: st.lane_enters is 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', st.travel_region the kind that carrier quantifier ranges over, st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' and st.highway the way itself as DEF-NRS-484A-095 defines it, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'; the two ways so read must not be the same way. st.lane_enters is read as the source's record and never inferred from a velocity, so the carriers are told apart by the map.

'the driver of the vehicle on the left' binds the subject: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the one in actual physical control, which the ontology reads through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the subject is the vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle claimed as one atom. 'on the left' is rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of", "immediately to the rear")', the atom the ontology names for exactly these words: the subject is the vehicle on the left where the other vehicle bears to the subject's right in the subject's own frame. The relation is read between the two vehicles the trigger binds, so no third road user of the scene can take the role.

'the vehicle on the right' is the other of the two vehicles the trigger binds, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, singled out by rel.bearing bearing to the subject's right in the subject's frame -- the words the atom's contract names. 'shall yield the right-of-way' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle ... approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not entering the junction at an observation at which the right-hand vehicle lies within it (drv.motion.region_entry on the subject, rel.occupies on the other, on the region of kind st.intersection the trigger binds), by not coming into contact with it (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap'), and by keeping clear of it while both are within the junction, which rel.surface_gap ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies, each body's footprint read with its own heading and extent'), prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance measure under constant velocities within the horizon, with kin.speed the subject's own speed. rel.surface_gap is not read as an order of arrival -- the order is already settled by the two entries the trigger reads -- and rel.contact is not a stand-in for a near miss, which is why the closest-approach primitives stand beside it.

The same words as in subsection 1 take the same atoms. 'official traffic-control devices' is DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic': the signals by dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head'), dev.lane_control_signal, dev.pedestrian_signal, dev.crossing_warning_signal and dev.railway_signal_or_gate; the signs by dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt'), dev.yield_sign, dev.regulatory_sign, dev.zone_sign and dev.speed_limit_sign; the markings by st.lane_marking and st.centre_line ('the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway'); the temporary devices by dev.temporary_traffic_control. 'at intersections controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', read on the junction the two vehicles enter or on the subject's own approach carrier, which rel.occupies, st.travel_region and st.lane_enters bind.

'vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions' is read as the ontology directs: rel.oncoming is 'not a stand-in for the direction a road user approaches from -- that is read through the carrier it approaches through, any carrier st.lane_enters admits, whose entrance end is the intersection, and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction) at the same instant'. Each vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is the same st.intersection (st.lane_enters), and the two carriers' designated directions are opposed: their normalised dot product is at or below the negative of p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance. The classes are the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom.

'is making a left turn' is drv.motion.left_turn, 'the road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning ... the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle ... to the left', read on either of the two vehicles as 'one of the vehicles' allows. The concept states the turning of the body only; no signal and no declared intention stands in for it, and the intention the same words also name is carried separately.

operationalizations.convention: Arrival-simultaneity convention: the two entries count as at approximately the same time where the interval between the observations at which each vehicle's footprint first comes to overlap the junction -- each read from kin.time, 'the instant of observation of a scene' -- is at most p.simultaneous_entry_window. The window is the headway within which two vehicles entering a junction from crossing highways are still both inside the junction's conflict area at ordinary approach speeds, so the closer the two entries the more surely the words hold and the farther apart the more surely they do not; it is the gap-acceptance figure for a crossing manoeuvre and not a figure of how much deference is enough.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn to the left at the region named as the declaration's target

applicability: The subject vehicle and another vehicle of the aggregate each enter one and the same intersection, each from a carrier lying on a highway other than the other's, and the two entry observations lie within p.simultaneous_entry_window of each other; the other vehicle bears to the subject's right in the subject's frame, so that the subject is the vehicle on the left. The duty does not apply where an official traffic-control device governs that junction or the subject's approach carrier -- unless either node of subsection 4 is engaged for the subject at that junction, which suspends that exception -- and it does not apply where the two carriers' designated directions are opposed and either vehicle is declared to intend a left turn at that junction or is making one.
obligation: From the entries on, the subject must grant precedence to the vehicle on its right: it must not enter the junction at an observation at which that vehicle lies within it, must not come into contact with it, and must not let its closest approach to it under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon fall below p.yield_min_clearance while that vehicle is within the junction.

narrowings.why: 'shall yield the right-of-way' is read as granting precedence in the three observable ways the definition's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' admits on a trace: no entry while the right-hand vehicle lies within the junction, no contact, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance. Where both vehicles are already within the junction the first of the three is spent and the other two carry the duty.
'the driver of the vehicle on the left' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.
'official' is read as the presence of the device on the road: the feature's presence is the observable evidence of its official status.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An unsignalised, unsigned crossing of two highways. A car and a van enter the junction within half a second of each other, each from a lane lying on a different highway, and the van bears to the car's right. The car keeps its speed, closes on the van inside the junction and the two bodies touch.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same crossing and the same two entries within half a second, the van again on the car's right. The car brakes immediately inside the junction, stays well clear of the van throughout and lets it pass: no contact and no closest approach within the horizon below the clearance bound.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car and the van enter the same junction from different highways, but eight seconds apart: the entries are not within the simultaneity window, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Both vehicles enter the junction within half a second from different highways, but the source does not report the direction of the van from the car in the car's frame, so which vehicle is on the left is unknown and the rule reports unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The two vehicles enter the same junction simultaneously from different highways, but a traffic signal governs the junction and is operating normally: the section does not apply at a junction controlled by an official traffic-control device and no node of subsection 4 is engaged.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The same signalised junction with its heads installed, uncovered and dark, so subsection 4 is engaged for the car and the device exception is suspended. The car and the van enter simultaneously from different highways, the van on the car's right, and the car drives into it.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A car on the left and a van on its right enter a junction simultaneously, but the two carriers they enter by have opposed designated directions and the source declares the car's current plan to be a left turn at that junction: the section does not apply.
