segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:
The driver of a vehicle
shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign,
in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1],
prior to entering an intersection
if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
although not a part of a through highway

and shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield and which are within the intersection or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: The same words as in subsection 1 take the same atoms. 'traffic' is DEF-NRS-484A-285's aggregate, claimed as the single atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role is police_officer, ...; indication is stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)', read with role police_officer, DEF-NRS-484A-180's 'officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic'; 'or a traffic-control signal' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head', the device by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed. The controlling is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection', read on the junction the subject approaches or its own approach carrier, which rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters and st.intersection bind to the subject's own approach.

'The driver of a vehicle' binds the subject: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the one who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. The mapping index maps the same words to the same atom.

'shall stop in obedience to a stop sign' is the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 defines, 'complete cessation from movement', carried by drv.motion.standstill within the speed tolerance its contract names, owed where dev.stop_sign -- the 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt' -- governs the subject's approach carrier; 'or yield in compliance with a yield sign' is owed where dev.yield_sign -- 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt' -- governs it instead, and is carried by kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed at the place. dev.governs gives 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', read on the carrier the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the junction (st.lane_enters, st.intersection), so the sign obeyed is the one governing this approach and not any sign of the scene. The place at which the act is owed is not read here: the reference span requires compliance with the manner subsection 1 prescribes, and that rule carries the stop line, the crosswalk and the view point in their order.

'prior to entering an intersection' fixes the event the act precedes: drv.motion.region_entry is 'the road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation ... the event of that coming to overlap', read on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'), with rel.occupies the anchor to the subject's own footprint. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line: the event is the entry into the junction, while the place of the act is the one subsection 1 prescribes, which lies earlier.

'a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto' is the presence of dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') governing at least one entrance of that junction: dev.governs gives 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end' -- so an entrance of the junction is such a carrier -- st.travel_region the kind those carrier quantifiers range over, st.intersection the junction, and rel.occupies the anchor tying the subject to the carrier it approaches through. No stop line or crossing is read here: the entrance is the carrier itself, not a mark upon it. The words' 'one or more entrances' is read over the entrances of that junction, so a sign at an entrance other than the subject's satisfies the condition, while which act the subject owes is read from the sign governing its own carrier.

residues.why: 'although not a part of a through highway' adds no observable condition to the duty: it is concessive, saying that the halt or the yielding is owed even where the junction is not part of a through highway, so the duty is the same whether or not the junction is part of one. Reading it as a condition would make the rule apply only at junctions off a through highway, which is narrower than the words.

applicability: The subject vehicle approaches an intersection -- it occupies a carrier whose entrance end is that junction -- and a stop sign or a yield sign governs at least one entrance of that junction, whether or not the junction is part of a through highway. The duty does not apply where a police officer is directing the traffic there or a traffic-control signal governs the junction or the approach.
obligation: Before the subject enters that intersection it must have obeyed the sign governing its own approach carrier, in the manner subsection 1 prescribes: a halt where that sign is a stop sign, a halt or a speed at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed where it is a yield sign, performed at the place subsection 1 names in its order -- the stop line marking that carrier, else the crosswalk marking it, else the point nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing way reaches the view distance -- which this node requires by composing that rule's verdict rather than restating its places. The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that junction; a halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of the governing mark, short of it and not overlapping the junction, counts at the place. The search for the act runs back from the entry observation and ends at the start of that approach -- the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, was off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance -- or at the subject's previous entry into the same junction, and at nothing else: not at another junction, not at the first observation of the recording, not at a distance travelled. Where the search finds the act the duty is met; where it reaches either end without it the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end, because the history begins before the recording or because the carrier's association with the mark or its direction is unobserved, the duty is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'yield in compliance with a yield sign' is read as a speed at the place at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed, the sign's own contract requiring 'yielding without a mandatory halt', together with the precedence the rest of the subsection states and the second node of this line carries. A reading that demanded a halt under a yield sign would hold the subject to more than the words.
'is erected' is read as the sign's presence on the road at an entrance of the junction: the feature's presence is the observable evidence of its erection by an authority.
'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A junction of two minor streets, neither a through highway, with stop signs at all four entrances and no officer or signal. A stop line marks the car's approach lane. The car rolls over the line at 5 m/s and enters the junction without its speed ever reaching the standstill tolerance on the approach.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same all-way stop junction. The car comes to rest with its speed at zero within the stop-point tolerance of the stop line marking its lane and short of it, then enters the junction. No other road user is in the scene and the verdict is decided.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same junction, but no stop sign or yield sign is erected at any of its entrances: the condition fails, so the rule is not engaged and the car's entry without halting is not judged here.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car enters the junction without halting and a stop sign stands beside its approach, but the source does not report which travel regions that sign governs, so whether a sign is erected at an entrance of this junction and which act the car owes are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A yield sign, not a stop sign, governs the car's approach to a minor-street junction with a yield sign at one other entrance. The car does not halt but comes down to 3 m/s within the stop-point tolerance of the yield line before entering: under a yield sign no mandatory halt is owed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A minor-street junction with stop signs at every entrance, the car's own included. Its lane's stop lines and crosswalks are observed and none marks the lane, so the manner rule puts the act at the point nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing street reaches the view distance. The car crosses that point at 6 m/s and enters the junction without ever halting.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already between its stop line and the junction, inside the line's stopping zone, and the car then enters the junction. No halt is recorded, and the recording holds neither the start of the approach upstream of the line nor a previous entry of the car into that junction.
scenarios.boundary: the stretch of the approach upstream of the stop line's stopping zone, at which the car entered that zone, lies before the first observation of the recording

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the complete cessation from movement DEF-NRS-484A-255 requires, set at the noise floor of a speed channel at rest.
param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed
param_proposals.convention: Yield-sign approach convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle at a yield-controlled entrance counts as having slowed, so that it can give way at the entrance without a mandatory halt; taken as the crawl speed design practice assigns to a yield-controlled approach.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book and MUTCD practice for yield-controlled approaches, where a 10 mph approach speed is the design basis for giving way without stopping.

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which an act counts as at the place the words name -- the stop line, the crosswalk or the view point -- covering the width of the marking and the position error of the body outline.
param_proposals.source: Marking-geometry and localisation practice: a transverse line about half a metre wide plus the position error of a body outline.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:
The driver of a vehicle
shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign, in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1], prior to entering an intersection
if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
although not a part of a through highway
and shall proceed cautiously,
yielding to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield and which are within the intersection
or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: The same words as in subsection 1 take the same atoms. 'traffic' is DEF-NRS-484A-285's aggregate, claimed as the single atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given', with role police_officer, DEF-NRS-484A-180's 'officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic'; 'or a traffic-control signal' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head', the device by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed. The controlling is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection', read on the junction the subject is at or on its own approach carrier, which rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters and st.intersection bind.

'The driver of a vehicle' binds the subject, and 'such driver' later in the sentence is the same one: the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. The mapping index maps the same words to the same atom.

'a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto' is the presence of dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') governing at least one entrance of that junction: dev.governs gives 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end' -- so an entrance of the junction is such a carrier -- st.travel_region the kind those carrier quantifiers range over, st.intersection the junction, and rel.occupies the anchor tying the subject to the carrier it approaches through. No stop line or crossing is read here: the entrance is the carrier itself, not a mark upon it.

'vehicles' are road users of the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom and quantified over inside the obligation. 'not so obligated to stop or yield' is read on the road: such a vehicle reached the junction through a carrier that no stop sign and no yield sign governs, which dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign and dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') decide on the carrier st.lane_enters gives ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), st.travel_region being the kind that quantifier ranges over and rel.occupies the anchor to that vehicle's own footprint; a carrier never takes the governance of a carrier it overlaps, so the sign read is the one recorded for its own carrier. 'which are within the intersection' is rel.occupies on the junction region of kind st.intersection. 'yielding' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not coming into contact with such a vehicle (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and by not letting its closest approach to it fall below the clearance, which prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance give under constant velocities within the horizon and rel.surface_gap measures between the nearest points of the bodies, with kin.speed the subject's own speed.

'during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection' fixes when the duty is read: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on the junction region of kind st.intersection gives the subject's being across or within it, and kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.standstill_speed_tolerance gives its moving. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line: the words name the junction itself.

operationalizations.convention: A low-speed stopping-distance convention bounds the caution: crossing the junction after obeying the sign, the subject's speed stays at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed, the speed at which a vehicle can be brought to rest within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to. The degree of the hazard enters through the conflict-avoidance convention, the closest approach under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon staying clear of p.yield_min_clearance, so that the bound moves with the proximity and closing speed of the road users the same sentence names rather than switching on their presence alone.

operationalizations.standard: or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance convention for a crossing from a sign-controlled entrance. 'So closely' is the other vehicle's distance to the junction, which st.region_geometry gives as 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', read on a vehicle on a carrier entering that junction (rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters): the vehicle is so close where that distance is at most its own speed (kin.speed) times p.yield_headway_time, so the bound moves with its speed -- a faster approach makes a greater distance count, a slower one a smaller. The immediacy is read in the same breath by the conflict-avoidance convention: the closest approach between the two bodies under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon falling below p.yield_min_clearance, measured between the nearest points of the bodies by rel.surface_gap. Both figures are the reading's, from gap-acceptance tables for a crossing manoeuvre.

residues.why: 'although not a part of a through highway' adds no observable condition: it is concessive, saying that the cautious proceeding and the yielding are owed even where the junction is not part of a through highway, so the duty is the same whether or not it is. Reading it as a condition would make the rule apply only at junctions off a through highway, which is narrower than the words.

applicability: A stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances of the intersection the subject is at, whether or not the junction is part of a through highway; the subject's footprint overlaps that junction and its speed is above p.standstill_speed_tolerance, so that it is moving across or within it. The duty does not apply where a police officer is directing the traffic there or a traffic-control signal governs the junction or the approach.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject is moving across or within that intersection it must proceed cautiously -- its speed at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed -- and must grant precedence to every vehicle of the aggregate whose approach carrier into that junction is governed by no stop sign and no yield sign and which either lies within the junction or approaches so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard: its distance to the junction at most its speed times p.yield_headway_time, or its closest approach to the subject under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon below p.yield_min_clearance. Granting precedence is: no contact with that vehicle, and no closest approach to it within p.yield_conflict_horizon below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'not so obligated to stop or yield' is read as a vehicle whose own approach carrier into that junction is governed by no stop sign and no yield sign: the obligation the words refer to is the one this subsection and subsection 1 place on a sign-controlled approach, and the sign governing the carrier is the observable fact that decides it. The rule is not read as composing another rule's verdict, since a rule counts as complied with where it is not engaged, which would say nothing about whether that vehicle was obligated.

'yielding' is read as granting precedence in the two observable ways open to a vehicle already moving across or within the junction: no contact with the privileged vehicle, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance.
'is erected' is read as the sign's presence on the road at an entrance of the junction: the feature's presence is the observable evidence of its erection by an authority.
'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the car's entrance to a junction where the crossing street's entrances carry no sign. The car halts, then pulls across the junction at 9 m/s while a van whose entrance carries no sign is within the junction, and the two bodies touch.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and stop sign. The car crosses the junction at 3 m/s and no other road user is in the scene at any observation: nothing is owed precedence, and the verdict is decided with the subject alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses a junction at which no stop sign and no yield sign is erected at any entrance: the condition fails and the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the junction while a van is within it, but the source does not report which travel regions the signs of the junction govern, so whether the van's approach was obligated to stop or yield is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the junction at 3 m/s while a van whose own entrance also carries a stop sign is within the junction: the van is itself obligated to stop, so it is not among the road users this duty protects, and no unobligated vehicle is near.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the junction at 3 m/s, below the cautious bound, while a van on the unsigned crossing street is twenty metres from the junction at 20 m/s -- within its speed times the headway bound -- and their closest approach under constant velocities within the horizon falls to a metre.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: No other road user is near, but the car crosses the junction at 12 m/s after halting at its stop sign: the cautious-proceeding bound is exceeded on its own.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the complete cessation from movement DEF-NRS-484A-255 requires, set at the noise floor of a speed channel at rest.
param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.cautious_proceed_max_speed
param_proposals.convention: Low-speed stopping-distance convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle crossing a junction from a sign-controlled entrance can be brought to rest within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to, taken as the 10 mph figure design practice uses for such an entry.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping-sight-distance table at low design speeds, and MUTCD practice treating a sign-controlled entry as a crawl speed.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_headway_time
param_proposals.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the headway, at the approaching vehicle's own speed, within which that vehicle is read as so close to the junction as to constitute an immediate hazard, being the time a crossing vehicle needs to clear its path.
param_proposals.source: Critical gap and follow-up headway practice for crossing manoeuvres (Highway Capacity Manual).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady yellow signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
is thereby warned that the related green movement is being terminated or that a steady red indication will be exhibited immediately thereafter,
and such vehicular traffic must not enter the intersection
when the red signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: 'the signal is a steady yellow signal alone' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head', read in its state circular_yellow: the enumeration lists circular_yellow for a steady yellow face, and since 'several states may be displayed at once', 'alone' is read as that state being displayed and no other state of the head being displayed at the observation. The atom is a device and not a sign, and no sign atom is claimed; the head read is the one governing the subject's approach, which the subject span binds.

'traffic' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-285 defines, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', admitted as the aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and claimed as one atom. The law's own word 'vehicular' qualifies it and limits which of its members the duty reads: of the classes the definition includes -- pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances -- the duty reads the vehicles, leaving out pedestrians and ridden or herded animals, so the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle is claimed beside it as the second class element, each as one atom and neither expanded into the classes it covers. 'facing the signal' is read as the ontology directs for an approach: the road user occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, st.intersection) and which the head governs, dev.governs being 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', with dev.traffic_signal the head itself. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and the facing is not read from the subject's heading: the ontology fixes which approach a road user is on by the carrier it occupies and that carrier's entrance, never by its velocity or heading.

'must not enter the intersection' is the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes, 'the road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation ... the event of that coming to overlap', read on the junction region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges') that the subject's carrier enters, with rel.occupies the anchor to the subject's own footprint and the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs. The concept is the entry and not the lying inside: a road user already within the junction when the red is exhibited makes no entry, which is what the words forbid. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line.

'when the red signal is exhibited' is dev.traffic_signal in its state circular_red, the enumeration's value for a steady red face, read on the same head that governs the subject's carrier (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), so that a red face governing another approach of the junction does not forbid this entry. The condition is read at the observation of the entry the obligation judges, since the words tie the exhibition to the moment of entering.

residues.why: 'is thereby warned that the related green movement is being terminated or that a steady red indication will be exhibited immediately thereafter' adds no observable condition to the prohibition: it states what the yellow face tells the driver, and the duty that follows is the same whether or not the green movement is in fact being terminated or the red in fact follows immediately. What a driver was warned of is a state of mind no trace carries, and reading the clause as a condition would make the rule apply only where the signal's programme is known, which is narrower than the words.

applicability: The subject is a road user of the traffic aggregate that is also a vehicle, occupying a carrier whose entrance end is an intersection and which a traffic-signal head governs, and that head displayed a steady circular yellow and no other state at the judged observation or at an earlier observation while the subject was on that carrier.
obligation: The subject must not enter that intersection -- its footprint must not come to overlap the junction region -- at an observation at which the head governing its carrier exhibits a steady circular red.

narrowings.why: The words join a trigger stated of the yellow face to a prohibition conditioned on the red face, which the head cannot display as its only state at one and the same observation. The prohibition is therefore read over the approach: the duty arises for a road user that faced the steady yellow alone on that carrier, and it forbids an entry made at an observation at which the governing head exhibits the red. A reading that required both faces at one observation would make the prohibition empty.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies a lane that enters a signalised junction, and the head governing that lane shows a steady circular yellow alone. Two seconds later the head shows circular red, and at that observation the car's footprint comes to overlap the junction region for the first time.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same lane and head. The car faces the steady yellow, brakes and comes to rest short of the junction, its footprint never overlapping the junction region while the head shows red; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head governing the car's lane shows a steady circular green throughout and never a steady yellow alone: the trigger never holds and the rule is not engaged, even though the car enters the junction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car faces the steady yellow and later enters the junction, but at the entry observation the source reports no state for the head governing its lane, so whether the red was exhibited is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car faces the steady yellow and crosses into the junction while the head still shows the yellow, the red appearing only after its whole body is inside: the entry was not made at an observation at which the red was exhibited.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on a crosswalk at the same junction faces the same head after it has shown steady yellow alone and steps into the junction region while the red is exhibited: the subject is not of the vehicle aggregate, so the duty this rule states does not bind it.

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
Both intersecting highways are two-directional:
The approach for a left turn must be made in that portion of the right half of the highway nearest the centerline thereof.

elements.justification: 'the driver of a vehicle' binds the subject: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the one who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), claimed as one atom and never expanded. The mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle' to the same atom.

'at an intersection' names the place the turn is intended at and the junction the approach leads to: st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', st.travel_region the kind that carrier quantifier ranges over, and rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the anchor that makes the junction the one the subject itself approaches. This element binds the region the declared intention of the preceding span is read at, and the same region the obligation's approach leads into. The trailing 'and:' only joins this condition to the next.

'two-directional' is the term DEF-NRS-484B-073 defines, used here in the copular form rather than as one contiguous phrase: 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'. 'undivided' is the absence of st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', on that way; 'upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions' is read from the designated directions of the carriers the way carries: st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in -- a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, bicycle lane or path, or a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder', opposed between two carriers of the way, their normalised dot product at or below the negative of p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance. st.highway is the way itself as DEF-NRS-484A-095 defines it, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority', st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', and st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on', which ties each carrier and each divider to its way. 'Both intersecting highways' are the two ways meeting at the junction the previous span binds: st.intersection with st.on_way, since 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there', and st.lane_enters with st.travel_region and rel.occupies pick out the subject's own way among them. st.median_or_divider is not read as a lane marking, and st.lane_direction is not read as a road user's heading.

'The approach for a left turn must be made in' is the subject's lateral place while it occupies the carrier whose entrance end is that junction: rel.occupies is the anchor, st.travel_region the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, st.lane_enters the entrance relation and st.intersection the junction. 'that portion of the right half of the highway nearest the centerline thereof' is read in the two ways the ontology provides for a way with and without marked lanes. Where the carriageway is laned, st.lane is 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles' and st.lane_adjacency carries the 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction': on a two-directional highway the leftmost lane of the subject's direction, read along st.lane_direction, is the portion of the right half nearest the centre line, so ordinal 1 for that direction is the portion the words name. Where no lane is recorded, st.centre_line is 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway' and prim.region_lateral_offset gives 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user': the centre line lies to the subject's left, its offset positive and of magnitude at least p.lateral_offset_resolution, which places the subject on the right half, and at most p.centerline_adjacent_distance, which is the portion nearest the centre line. st.roadway, st.highway and st.on_way bind the way and its improved part; st.lane_adjacency is expressly not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes, and none is read as one; st.lane is not a stand-in for a half of the roadway, which is why the unlaned case is read through the centre line and the lateral offset rather than through a lane ordinal; the primitive's own inputs are not claimed beside it.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn to the left at the region named as the declaration's target

applicability: The subject vehicle occupies a carrier whose entrance end is an intersection; the source declares its current plan to be a left turn at that intersection; and both the way carrying that carrier and the other way meeting at that junction are two-directional -- no physical barrier or dividing section lies on either, and each carries two carriers whose designated directions are opposed.
obligation: At every observation on that approach the subject must lie in the portion of the right half of its highway nearest the centre line: it occupies the lane of ordinal 1 for its own direction of travel, counted along that lane's designated direction, or, where the carriageway carries no recorded lane, the centre line of its roadway lies to its left with a signed lateral offset of at least p.lateral_offset_resolution and at most p.centerline_adjacent_distance.

narrowings.why: 'The approach for a left turn' restricts the duty to an approach made for a turn to the left: the condition span carries a declared intention to turn, and the obligation's own words select the left turn among the turns the earlier words allow, so the duty is read only where the declaration is a left turn at that junction.

'that portion of the right half of the highway nearest the centerline thereof' is read, where the carriageway is laned, as the lane of ordinal 1 for the subject's direction -- the leftmost lane of that direction and so the one adjoining the centre line -- and, where no lane is recorded, as a place whose signed lateral offset to the centre line is positive and at most p.centerline_adjacent_distance. The second bound is a width the reading sets, since the words name a portion and no measure of it; it is set at a design lane width, so that the portion read is the width of one line of vehicles beside the centre line.

'are allowed to proceed in opposite directions' is read as the designated directions of the carriers the way carries being opposed: a permission granted by an authority is nothing a scene displays, and the designated direction of travel on the road is its observable evidence.
'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A four-lane undivided street, two lanes each way, meets another undivided two-way street. The source declares the car's plan to be a left turn at that junction, and the car runs the whole approach in the kerbside lane -- ordinal 2 of its direction -- up to the junction.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same geometry and the same declared left turn. The car runs the approach in the lane of ordinal 1 for its direction, the one adjoining the centre line, throughout. No other road user is in the scene and the verdict is decided.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car approaches the same junction in the kerbside lane, but the source's current plan for it is to go straight through: no left turn is declared at that junction, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car approaches the junction with a declared left turn, but the source does not report the lane ordinals of the carriageway and the roadway carries a recorded lane, so which portion of the right half the car occupies is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A narrow two-way street with no lanes recorded, meeting another undivided two-way street. The car, declared to turn left at the junction, runs the approach with the centre line two metres to its left, inside the centre-line portion.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car, declared to turn left, approaches a junction on a highway divided by a raised median: the way is not two-directional in the definition's sense, so this paragraph does not apply.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: An unlaned two-way street, the car declared to turn left at the junction, running the whole approach close to the kerb with the centre line six metres to its left, outside the centre-line portion.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two directions still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees; its negative is the bound at which two directions are read as opposed.
param_proposals.source: The thirty-degree sector convention used for same-direction and opposed-direction tests in traffic conflict analysis.

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_offset_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Lateral-offset convention: the magnitude of a signed lateral offset below which the side a region lies on is not distinguishable from the measurement noise of the boundary and the position.
param_proposals.source: Map and localisation practice for boundary polygons in scene-graph traces.

param_proposals.name: p.centerline_adjacent_distance
param_proposals.convention: Lane-position convention: the lateral distance from the centre line within which a place on the right half of a two-directional highway counts as the portion nearest the centre line, set at one design lane width, the width of a single line of vehicles beside the centre line.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book design lane widths for urban arterials (3.0 to 3.6 m).

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle within an intersection intending to turn to the left shall yield the right-of-way to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction which is within the intersection or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver, having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: 'having given a signal' is the signal the left-turning vehicle emits: sig.turn_indicator, whose 'state is off, left or right: neither indicator lit, or the left or the right one', shown as left, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning is no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter', given as left. sig.turn_indicator is 'not a stand-in for the turn or lane change itself', and it is not used for one here: the turn is carried separately by its own concept in c3, and this span carries only the indication. 'when and as required' is read through the signalling convention: a left indication at some observation in the window p.turn_signal_advance_window behind the turn's recognition. The condition is read on the left-turning vehicle the obligation quantifies over, not on the subject.

'may make such left turn' names the manoeuvre drv.motion.left_turn denotes, 'the road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning ... the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle ... to the left', read on the left-turning vehicle while its footprint overlaps the junction: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on a region of kind st.intersection ties the turn to the junction the subject approaches, so that a left turn made elsewhere in the scene does not raise this duty. The concept states the turning of the body only, and neither a signal nor a declared intention stands in for it.

'the drivers of all other vehicles' binds the subject: the driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the subject is each other vehicle of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'approaching the intersection' is the ontology's own reading, 'a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters)', with st.travel_region the kind that carrier quantifier ranges over and st.intersection the junction at which the left turn is made. 'from the opposite direction' is read, as the ontology directs for these words, through that carrier's designated direction st.lane_direction being opposed to the direction of the carrier by which the left-turning vehicle reached the junction, their normalised dot product at or below the negative of p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance; rel.oncoming is expressly not a stand-in for the direction a road user approaches from, and the left-turning vehicle's heading swings through its turn, so the carriers and not the headings are read.

'the vehicle making the left turn' refers to the road user c3 already binds -- the vehicle of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed here as one atom, whose left turn in that junction c3's element carries with its concept -- so the obligation reads that same road user and re-claims no manoeuvre of its own: the turning is the condition that raises the duty, and the duty itself is conduct of the subject towards it. Its presence in the junction is rel.occupies on a region of kind st.intersection. 'shall yield the right-of-way' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not coming into contact with that vehicle (rel.contact) and by not letting its closest approach to it fall below the clearance, which prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance give under constant velocities within the horizon and rel.surface_gap measures between the nearest points of the bodies, with kin.speed the subject's own speed. rel.contact is not a stand-in for a near miss, which is why the primitives stand beside it.

applicability: There is a vehicle t of the aggregate within an intersection making a left turn there, which has complied with the duty of NRS_484B_253_o1 ('having so yielded') and has given a left indication, by indicator or by arm signal, at some observation in the window p.turn_signal_advance_window behind the recognition of its turn; and the subject vehicle occupies a carrier whose entrance end is that intersection and whose designated direction is opposed to the direction of t's approach carrier.
obligation: At every such observation the subject must grant precedence to t: it must not come into contact with t, and must not let its closest approach to t under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon fall below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'shall yield the right-of-way' is read as granting precedence in the two observable ways open here: no contact with the turning vehicle, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance.
'the drivers of all other vehicles' is read through each vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A van within a junction has yielded to the opposing stream, shows its left indicator through the two seconds before its turn is recognized, and turns left. The subject car occupies the opposing approach lane entering the same junction and drives on into the van's path, the two bodies touching.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and the same signalled, yielded left turn by the van. The subject car brakes on its approach and stays more than ten metres clear of the van throughout, no closest approach within the horizon coming near the clearance bound.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car occupies the opposing approach lane of a junction in which no vehicle is making a left turn at all: no road user raises the duty, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A van makes a signalled left turn in the junction the subject approaches, but the source does not report whether the van's footprint overlaps the junction region, so whether the turn is the one made in that intersection is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The van turns left in the junction and has yielded to the opposing stream, but its indicator stays off and it gives no arm signal in the window behind the recognition of the turn: the weaker fact -- a turn made without the signal the words require -- leaves the other drivers' duty unraised, and the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The van signals left and turns, but it did not comply with its own duty to yield under the first node of this section: it turned across an oncoming vehicle that was within the junction. Having not so yielded, it raises no duty on the other drivers.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two directions still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees; its negative is the bound at which two directions are read as opposed.
param_proposals.source: The thirty-degree sector convention used for same-direction and opposed-direction tests in traffic conflict analysis.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_signal_advance_window
param_proposals.convention: Signalling convention: the window behind the movement within which an indication counts as the signal given for it, taken from the advance-notice practice for a turn.
param_proposals.source: Driver-signalling practice and the advance-notice intervals of state vehicle codes.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_onset_yaw_rate
param_proposals.convention: Manoeuvre-onset convention: the rate of change of heading above which a body is read as turning rather than running straight, set above the yaw noise of a vehicle holding its lane.
param_proposals.source: Yaw-rate channel noise and lane-keeping figures from instrumented-vehicle studies.

param_proposals.name: p.left_turn_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn-recognition convention: the heading change accumulated since the onset at which a turn to the left is recognized as made, rather than as a lane change or a bend taken.
param_proposals.source: Manoeuvre-recognition practice: half the ninety-degree heading change of a right-angle junction turn.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.
